short_description: Heavily rebuilt cardiomyocyte of the ventricular conduction system: a fat, pale, glycogen-stuffed muscle cell that traded most of its contractile machinery for connexin-40 gap junctions, making it the fastest-conducting cell in the heart (~2-4 m/s) so both ventricles contract as one.
do_not_draw: a neuron: no dendrites, no axon, no myelin, no Nodes of Ranvier, no synapses
the cerebellar Purkinje NEURON (flask-shaped soma with a flat espaliered dendritic tree) - a different cell that only shares the name
a densely striated working cardiomyocyte with full-width edge-to-edge sarcomere banding
a cell thinner than the surrounding working myocytes (Purkinje cells are wider)
nuclei flattened against the sarcolemma (they sit centrally in the clear zone)
cell wall, nucleoid, plasmids, chloroplasts, large central vacuole, flagellum, cilia
a branching star-shaped or tree-like cell outline
sparks, lightning bolts, arrows or glowing signal trails in the scientific styles
any baked-in text, letters, numbers, labels, scale bars or watermarks
colour_note: Colour here is teaching convention. In H&E the Purkinje cells stain conspicuously PALER than the strongly eosinophilic working myocardium, so the palette keeps a pale cream/straw cell body with a warm rose-pink working myocyte for contrast; glycogen = soft amber granules, myofibrils = deeper rose bands at the rim, nuclei = muted blue-violet, gap junctions = teal, mitochondria = warm orange, endocardium = pale grey-blue. The same mapping is used in all four styles.
